question: Can a source-only illuminant-chromaticity-conditioned convex bank of bounded explicit LUTs recover held synthetic camera normalization better than global and affine controls, and does an exact same-chromaticity/different-spectrum control prove that chromaticity alone is not an identifying nuisance observation?

primary_source.title: Illuminant-Adaptive 3D Lookup Tables for Camera Color Correction

clean_room_scope.mechanism: source-only normalized white-point r,g selects nonnegative sum-to-one weights over bounded explicit residual LUTs; final RGB is deterministic trilinear LUT evaluation
clean_room_scope.difference_from_source: synthetic full-LUT and SVD-basis capacity/identifiability test, not a reproduction of the paper's Tucker factors, MLP, cameras, spectra or datasets

stop_rules: Do not alter the fixture, descriptors, rank, baselines, metrics or thresholds after any score.
A capacity pass cannot establish illuminant or camera identifiability when the same-chromaticity hidden-spectrum control fails.
Do not rescue same-chromaticity ambiguity with target pixels, application outcomes, scene identity, stock labels or a post-score descriptor.
A result may only guide future source-normalization evidence design; it cannot promote a film look, calibrated camera correction or product path.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic clean-room mechanism capacity and information-sufficiency evidence for a bounded explicit source-normalization operator; not camera calibration, real illuminant recovery, film/stock response, photographic quality or product promotion.
